title: Apple Loaf Cake
subtitle: A moist, fruit-packed loaf with grated apple
excerpt: Grated apple melts into the batter as it bakes, keeping the crumb soft and adding a gentle sweetness. This loaf needs no decoration and no frosting. It travels well and keeps for several days.
sourceNotes: Fruit loaf cakes are a long tradition in British baking. Grated apple as a moistening ingredient became common in home baking throughout the twentieth century as a lower-sugar alternative to dried fruit.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice and freeze individually wrapped for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps wrapped at room temperature for 4 to 5 days. Flavour improves on day two.

content.text: Grate the apple and fold it in without squeezing out the juice. The moisture is what makes this loaf stay tender.
Heat the oven to 180C. Grease a 900g loaf tin and line with baking paper.
Whisk the melted butter, eggs, milk, and honey together in a large bowl.
Fold in the flour until just combined.
Fold in the grated apple. The batter will be thick.
Spoon into the prepared tin. Level the top.
Bake for 50 to 55 minutes. Test with a skewer. It should come out clean.
Leave to cool in the tin for 10 minutes. Then turn out onto a rack.

items.symptom: Loaf is very wet inside even after full bake time.
items.cause: Apples had very high water content, or tin was too small.
items.fix: Use a standard 900g tin. Add 5 to 10 minutes if still wet.

items.symptom: Top browns too fast before centre is set.
items.cause: Oven runs hot or rack too high.
items.fix: Lay a sheet of foil loosely over the top halfway through baking.

items.cause: Underbaked or too much liquid from the apple.
items.fix: Always test with a skewer before pulling the tin from the oven.
